title: Triangle Angle Theorems: Angle Sum, Exterior Angles, and Isosceles Triangles
seo_title: Triangle Angle Sum and Exterior Angle Theorem Worksheet (Geometry) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on triangle angle theorems: the angle sum, the Exterior Angle Theorem, solving for x, and isosceles and equilateral triangles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The angles of a triangle add to 180°.
key_sub: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent.
body_html:
How it works

Triangle Angle Sum Theorem: the three interior angles of a triangle add to 180°.

Exterior Angle Theorem: an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles (the two that are not next to it).

Isosceles Triangle Theorem: if two sides are congruent, the angles opposite them (the base angles) are congruent. An equilateral triangle has three 60° angles.

The acute angles of a right triangle add to 90°.

Example

A triangle has angles (2x + 10)°, (3x)° and (x + 20)°. Find the largest angle.

6x + 30 = 180, so x = 25

Angles: 60°, 75°, 45°

Answer: 75°

Example

An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 40°. Find each base angle.

180 %s 40 = 140

140 ÷ 2 = 70

Answer: 70°

Common mistakes

  • Using 360° instead of 180° for the angles of a triangle.
  • Adding the interior angle next to the exterior angle. Use the two remote angles.
  • Treating the vertex angle as a base angle. The base angles are opposite the congruent sides.
  • Stopping at x when the question asks for an angle.

faq.q: What do the angles of a triangle add up to?
faq.a: 180 degrees. This is the Triangle Angle Sum Theorem.

faq.q: What is the Exterior Angle Theorem?
faq.a: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it.

faq.q: What are the base angles of an isosceles triangle?
faq.a: The two angles opposite the congruent sides. They are always congruent.

faq.q: Can a triangle have two right angles?
faq.a: No. Two right angles already add to 180 degrees, leaving nothing for the third angle.
